findings.rule: REVIEW.md: no test edits in a fix task
findings.summary: pre-existing test file modified in a fix-type change (REVIEW.md framework rule; build guide step 25)

findings.rule: spec R3: urllib_fetch opens only https:// URLs, refusing other schemes before any socket opens
findings.summary: If the environment's http_proxy (or ftp_proxy) names an https:// proxy, ProxyHandler.proxy_open re-types the http/ftp request to https and re-enters the opener, so _HTTPSHandler sends it to the proxy instead of UnknownHandler refusing it, and test_only_https_urls_are_opened would then open a socket to that proxy; inferred from CPython's ProxyHandler, not run (the sandbox denied the check), uncommon configuration, and reachable only by a direct urllib_fetch call since the layer builds only https URLs.

findings.rule: REVIEW.md framework rules: flag when the change has made CLAUDE.md outdated
findings.summary: The diff makes CLAUDE.md's Setup line (no longer enough for Windows) and 'the one runtime dependency is polars>=1.0' outdated; plan.md names both edits and sdlc.yaml commands.setup for the owner as spec R12 requires, so graded a nit, with the doubt that the rule may want it tracked until the owner's guardrail PR lands after this merges.

findings.rule: REVIEW.md framework rules: in a fix-type change the diff must not modify test files that existed before the fix
findings.summary: In a fix-type change the pre-existing file tests/test_data.py gains imports and four appended tests; no existing test is edited and the additions sit in the first, reproducing commit as the intent and plan require, so this is graded a nit, with the doubt that REVIEW.md's wording ('test files that existed before the fix') could be read literally as a breach.
